# Issue344 owned Windows complete-package QA — QA5 SOURCE proposal

This bundle is not deployment, npm publication, a successful Windows run, or Dell Excel acceptance. The management owner supplies only exact source/license artifacts after the normal complete OpenClaw build/package and exact focused native 695-unit + two-owned-fixture proof have passed. The closed generic eligibility schema binds four immutable source/build proof hashes and rejects unknown top-level/nested private fields. It fixes deploymentReady=false and the canonical gate as pending separate live acceptance. Missing hashes, unfinished required source/focused-native gates, missing owned-fixture cases, incomplete source-policy bundled plugin set, or a placeholder eligibility receipt are refused before installation.

This QA5 successor preserves verified runtime/native/complete-OpenClaw identities and now binds the actual normally repacked license-corrected SDK/native tar hashes and measured byte counts, plus the exact immutable SDK build receipt. Final source freeze records these measured source proofs, not a package transfer or Windows acceptance. Historical local records are retained unchanged under `history/v3/` and `history/v4/` and never counted as new QA5 checks. Windows package execution, transfer and live/Excel acceptance are unperformed here.

## Retention and failure ownership

Management source tars/verified native root remain leased to their original owner. Prepared copies and upload readback files are reproducible work: uploader removes each verified readback immediately but keeps hashes and journal. After actual Actions artifacts are independently verified and the parent releases the lease, remove only that declared generated copy root; original source/receipt/native leases are not this bundle's cleanup authority. Internal QA prerelease assets remain until their owner explicitly closes that transfer retention; no delete action is included.

Windows owns one GUID root under LocalAppData Temp on C:\; it writes an ownership receipt and retains every failed/outcome-unknown state. Native fixture files clean only their own exact leaves as authored. No recursive failure cleanup or retries. Successful expanded root is uploaded with hidden files and retained until artifact handover, then ephemeral runner disposal handles that runner. Evidence is outside the seal inventory, and result receipts explicitly deny live/Excel acceptance.

Required future Windows5.1/native/package/transfer runs are **unrun** until the owner dispatches and verifies them. Canonical all/GUI/no-skips is still required separately before any LIVE acceptance; this package-only run never makes deploymentReady=true. Source review is not proof of prerelease readability, normal installation, ABI on Windows, full expanded seal acceptance, real task fences, or Excel behavior.
